plan.title: ci: taskfile_release_names test intermittently hangs the merge gate (spawns the real release task chain)

narratives.Description: taskfile_release_names.test.ts runs real task release calls that pull in ts:build, the engine wrapper and the pinned runtime with no time limit, and twice on 2026-11-20 one of them never returned and held the merge gate. The fix, bound by the design-critique lean in comment 7044705026, runs go-task against a temp fixture built from the real tasks/engine.yml, tasks/engine-invoke.cjs and release ENGINE_CMD with a stub dist/bin.js, and puts a 30 s limit on every task spawn in the file. The #2547 apostrophe regression stays covered, and no build or release pipeline runs from this file.
narratives.Overview:
1. Fixture helper (P1, P2). A test helper builds a temp dir with copies of the real `tasks/engine.yml` and `tasks/engine-invoke.cjs` in `tasks/`, a stub `dist/bin.js` that prints `JSON.stringify(process.argv.slice(2))`, and a `Taskfile.yml` that includes `engine: ./tasks/engine.yml` and has one `release` task calling `engine:invoke` with the `ENGINE_CMD` value read from the real `Taskfile.yml` `release` task, with no `deps`. If the real `release` task or its `ENGINE_CMD` is missing, the helper fails the test.
2. #2547 test (P1, P2). Runs `task -t <fixture>/Taskfile.yml release -- 0.0.0 --dry-run --summary "test what's next"`, expects exit 0, and asserts the printed argv has `--summary` followed by `test what's next` as one element.
3. Help dispatch test (P1, P4). Replaces the real `release -- --help` call with a fixture run of `release -- --help` and asserts the printed argv starts with `release` and contains `--help`. It is named as dispatch coverage.
4. Delete the old full dry-run test (P1). No nightly copy.
5. Bounded runner (P3). Every `task` spawn in the file, the `task --version` probe included, goes through one helper with a 30 s limit and `killSignal: "SIGKILL"`. Over the limit, the test (or, for the probe, the file) fails with a message that the command exceeded 30 s and was terminated. The probe skips the tests only when the `task` executable is missing (`ENOENT`).
6. Evidence in the PR (P2, P3, P4). The positive run and a failing run with `{{.ENGINE_CMD}}` wrapped in single quotes in the invoke script of `tasks/engine.yml`, both on Linux; one Linux run of the runner against a child that leaves a grandchild holding the output pipe, with its return time and message; the file vitest time before (4254 ms in job 136352833330; hung in run 44683125022) and after.

## Acceptance Criteria

- In `taskfile_release_names.test.ts`, no test runs the repository `release` task from `Taskfile.yml` or its `ts:build` dependency; the release tests run go-task against a temp fixture with the real `tasks/engine.yml`, `tasks/engine-invoke.cjs` and release `ENGINE_CMD`, and a stub `dist/bin.js`.
- The #2547 test asserts that `test what's next` arrives as one argv element after `--summary`, and the help dispatch test asserts that `--help` reaches the stub after `release`.
- The fixture helper fails the test when `Taskfile.yml` has no `release` task or no `ENGINE_CMD` in it.
- Wrapping `{{.ENGINE_CMD}}` in single quotes in the invoke script of `tasks/engine.yml` makes the #2547 test fail on Linux, and the PR records the passing and failing runs.
- Every `task` spawn in the file, the `task --version` probe included, has a 30 s limit; over the limit it fails with a message that names the command and the limit; only a missing `task` executable skips.
- The PR records a Linux run in which a child leaves a grandchild holding the output pipe and the runner returns at the limit with that message.
- The file finishes in under 10 s in CI, and the PR records its vitest time before (4254 ms in job 136352833330; hung in run 44683125022) and after.
narratives.Constraint:
- Keeping the real `release -- --help` call with only a timeout (comment 7044680806, finding 1: the build stays in the file and a cold build cannot meet 10 s).
- A probe timeout inside the existing catch, which would turn a hang into skipped tests (comment 7044680806, finding 2).
- A hard-coded copy of the release `ENGINE_CMD` in the fixture (comment 7044680806, finding 4).
- Moving the full dry run to a nightly or slow lane (Stop 1 exclusion; CONTRIBUTING § Slow tests).
narratives.UserStory: As a Directive maintainer waiting on the merge gate, I want taskfile_release_names.test.ts to test the #2547 quoting path against a small go-task fixture with bounded spawns, so that the file can no longer hold the merge gate while the #2547 regression stays covered.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
- Fixture helper and bounded runner: in packages/core/src/content-contracts/standards/taskfile_release_names.test.ts add a helper that builds the temp fixture (copies of tasks/engine.yml and tasks/engine-invoke.cjs, a stub dist/bin.js that prints its argv as JSON, and a Taskfile.yml whose release task calls engine:invoke with the ENGINE_CMD read from the real Taskfile.yml release task, no deps; the helper fails the test when that task or its ENGINE_CMD is missing), and one bounded runner (spawnSync, 30 s timeout, killSignal SIGKILL, a timeout message naming the command and the limit). The task --version probe uses the runner and skips only on ENOENT. The helper stays in the test file, so the story adds no production module.
- Tests: replace the #2547 dry run and the real release -- --help call with fixture runs that assert the argv the stub prints; keep the --list-all name tests, now through the bounded runner; delete the old full dry-run test with no nightly copy.
- Evidence for the PR body: on Linux, the positive run, a failing run with {{.ENGINE_CMD}} wrapped in single quotes in the invoke script of tasks/engine.yml (a local edit, not committed), a runner run against a child whose grandchild holds the output pipe (return time and message), and the file vitest time before and after from the PR merge-gate log.
- Changelog: one fragment changelog.d/6862-release-names-test-hang.md, one line, no file paths, referencing #6862.

## In plain English
One test in `taskfile_release_names.test.ts` (the #2547 apostrophe test) runs the whole `task release` pipeline in dry-run mode: go-task, a TypeScript build, the engine wrapper, then the pinned runtime. It has no timeout. Usually the whole file takes about 4 seconds, but twice on 2026-11-20 that call never returned and held the merge gate (one job was cancelled after 6 hours). The recommended fix tests the #2547 quoting path directly against a tiny fixture that uses the real engine wiring and a stub binary, so no build or pipeline runs, and puts a timeout on every `task` call left in the file.

Root cause (corrected before this write-back; the issue body was edited to match):
- The first guess was that the dry run, lacking `--skip-ci`, runs a nested `task check`. It does not: with `--dry-run`, release step 5 only prints a DRYRUN line (`packages/core/src/release/pipeline.ts` 343-381). A local timed run took 27 s, about 25 s of it a cold `tsc -b` from the `ts:build` dependency, and printed every step as DRYRUN.
- The cost is not steady. Of the 43 latest completed merge-gate jobs, 42 finished in 12 min or less (median 6.4 min); in sampled job 136352833330 this file took 4254 ms.
- It is an intermittent hang. Run 44683125022 was cancelled at the 6 h limit with 1621 of 1622 files done and only this file in flight; pin PR #6861 (job 136381045739) shows the same state after 50 min. In the cancelled log the `release -- --help` call output is printed, and `execFileSync` prints a child stderr only after the child exits, so the stuck call came after it: the `--list-all` call or the #2547 dry run.
- Not known: which process in the chain blocks. At the cancel a node, node, sh chain was still alive and no nested `task` process was listed. The fix does not depend on that answer.

Operator decisions (Scott, 2026-11-20, relayed by the coordinator):
- Goal: "we need to speed up the pr runs as well", and "we want speed but still need testing".
- Keep the #2547 regression covered: a broken `ENGINE_CMD` quote must still fail a test.
- Ship in the next release: small scope, buildable in one PR.
- Prefer designs that remove work over designs that add gates.
- Out of this arc: other slow tests, the #6850 lifecycle fast lane, Go retirement (#6863), and the nightly lane itself (#6849).

## Pains
- P1 — The merge gate no longer runs a full `task release` pipeline from this file.
- P2 — The #2547 regression stays covered: wrapping `ENGINE_CMD` in single quotes inside the `engine:invoke` script (the pre-#2547 shape) still fails a test.
- P3 — A stuck `task` subprocess in this file fails its test within a fixed limit, with a message that names the command and the limit, instead of holding the gate.
- P4 — The file finishes in under 10 s in CI, and the PR records its before and after times.

## Excluded (not pains, not in this arc)
- Other slow or spawn-heavy tests, the #6850 lifecycle fast lane, #6863, and the #6849 nightly lane (operator-scoped out above).
- Moving a full release dry run to a nightly or slow lane. CONTRIBUTING § Slow tests (200-213) says no slow lane exists and forbids hiding flaky tests behind one.
- A `timeout-minutes` on the merge-gate job in `ci.yml`, and finding which process in the chain blocks. Both are possible later issues; neither is needed to stop this file holding the gate.

## Constraints (not pains)
- One PR. Changes stay in `taskfile_release_names.test.ts` (and a test helper if needed). No change to `Taskfile.yml`, `tasks/engine.yml`, `tasks/engine-invoke.cjs` or `ci.yml`.
- No new gate, check, policy flag or CI job.

## Anchors at the dispatch SHA
- `packages/core/src/content-contracts/standards/taskfile_release_names.test.ts` 23-35 (`--list-all` helper, `execFileSync`, no timeout), 52-66 (`release -- --help`, skipped on win32), 83-111 (#2547: `spawnSync` of `task release -- 0.0.0 --dry-run --skip-tag --skip-release --summary "test what's next"`, no timeout).
- `Taskfile.yml` 797-806: `release` has `deps: [ts:build]` and `ENGINE_CMD: 'release --project-root "{{.USER_WORKING_DIR}}" {{.CLI_ARGS}}'`. `tasks/ts.yml` 9-14: `build` runs `pnpm run build` (`tsc -b` plus bundle).
- `tasks/engine.yml` 13-14 (`DEFT_ROOT` is the parent of the `tasks/` folder), 62-72 (`invoke`; `DEFT_ENGINE_CMD_JSON: '{{ .ENGINE_CMD | toSlash | toJson }}'`), 108-114 (no buildable source and `DEFT_ROOT/dist/bin.js` present: `engine-invoke.cjs vendored "$bin"`).
- `tasks/engine-invoke.cjs` 13-15 (Node built-ins only), 349-366 (reads `DEFT_ENGINE_CMD_JSON`, `shellSplit`).
- `git show e9943a9bb^:tasks/engine.yml` 200-202: the pre-#2547 script had `engine_cmd='{{.ENGINE_CMD}}'`.
- `tasks/engine-invoke.test.cjs` 84-90 and 185-200: unit tests of `shellSplit` with apostrophes; they do not run go-task or `engine.yml`.
- `packages/core/src/release/pipeline.test.ts` 185 and 416: in-process `runPipeline` dry-run coverage.
- `vitest.config.ts` 294, 304, 336: test timeout 20 s on Linux; it cannot interrupt a synchronous spawn.

## Recommended mechanism (the thing to critique)
- R1 (P1, P2). Replace the #2547 test. A helper builds a temp fixture: copies of the real `tasks/engine.yml` and `tasks/engine-invoke.cjs` in `<tmp>/tasks/`, a stub `<tmp>/dist/bin.js` that prints `JSON.stringify(process.argv.slice(2))`, and `<tmp>/Taskfile.yml` that includes `engine: ./tasks/engine.yml` and has a `release` task calling `engine:invoke` with the `ENGINE_CMD` value read from the real `Taskfile.yml` `release` task (no `deps`). The test runs `task -t <tmp>/Taskfile.yml release -- 0.0.0 --dry-run --summary "test what's next"`, expects exit 0, and asserts the printed argv has `--summary` followed by `test what's next` as one element. The fixture has no `packages/` tree, so `engine.yml` takes its `dist/bin.js` branch: no build, no pin, no pipeline.
- R2 (P1). Delete the old full dry-run test. No nightly copy: the pipeline dry run is covered in-process (anchor above).
- R3 (P3). One helper runs every `task` spawn in the file with a `timeout` (120 s, which covers a cold `ts:build` in the `--help` test) and `killSignal: "SIGKILL"`. On `ETIMEDOUT` it fails with a message such as `task release -- --help did not exit within 120 s and was killed`.
- R4 (P4). The PR records the file's vitest time before (4254 ms in job 136352833330; hung in run 44683125022) and after, from its own merge-gate log.

Parent measurement (local, Windows, go-task 3.50.0, not CI): a prototype of the R1 fixture ran in 360 ms and printed `--summary`, `test what's next` as separate argv elements. With the fixture's `engine.yml` changed to wrap `{{.ENGINE_CMD}}` in single quotes in the invoke script, the same command exited 201 with `reached EOF without closing quote`. With the bare inline form `node "$bin" {{.ENGINE_CMD}}` it passed, because go-task quotes `CLI_ARGS` itself, so R1 guards the single-quote-wrap class, not every inline form.

Questions for the critic:
1. Is the root cause above proven enough to bind this fix, given that the blocking process is not identified?
2. Does R1 still catch #2547? Is reading `ENGINE_CMD` from the real `Taskfile.yml` worth it, or should the fixture hard-code it? Will the fixture behave the same on Linux CI and on Windows?
3. Does R3 fail with a clear message in the hang seen in CI? Node closes its pipe ends when a `spawnSync` timeout fires, so a grandchild that holds the pipe should not hold the test; the parent has not measured that on Linux.
4. The `release -- --help` test still runs the `ts:build` and pin chain. Should it stay in the merge gate with R3's timeout, or change too?

model: gpt-6
```quarantined
role: critic
```
audit-targets: none

## In plain English

The proposed fixture is a sound way to preserve the apostrophe regression test while removing the release pipeline. Identifying the exact hung process is unnecessary to justify that change.

The design needs one substantive adjustment: retaining the real release-help invocation retains its build dependency, so the proposed replacement alone does not support the under-10-second goal. Timeout handling also needs to include the availability probe without turning a timeout into skipped tests.

This review used pinned source reads at `f1b769a4a832c4ef8b223a8e82428741fd6608ec`. No tests, builds, or network requests were run. The reported CI timings and Windows prototype results remain parent-supplied evidence.

### 1. blocks-the-design — The retained help test preserves the expensive build path

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/content-contracts/standards/taskfile_release_names.test.ts:52–66` invokes the real `release -- --help`. `Taskfile.yml:797–806` gives that task an unconditional `ts:build` dependency; `tasks/ts.yml:9–14` dispatches the build script. The snapshot reports approximately 25 seconds for a cold build.

**Failure mode:** R1 removes the build from the apostrophe test, but the same file still invokes it through the help test. A 120-second timeout limits a failure; it does not make a successful cold build fit within 10 seconds. A warm CI measurement could conceal this retained dependency.

**Disposition consequence:** The design cannot bind as an unconditional P4 remedy while retaining that invocation unchanged. Prefer replacing it with a fixture assertion that the real release command template transports `--help` correctly, and describe the resulting coverage accurately as dispatch coverage. A stub printing “usage” would not test real CLI help.

The strongest case for retaining the test is its broader build/pin/help integration coverage. That would change my verdict if the scope explicitly accepted that cost and narrowed P4 to a measured warm-CI target. Under the stated speed goal, removing the dependency is the stronger choice.

### 2. sharpens-framing — Availability detection must distinguish absence from timeout

**Evidence:** `taskfile_release_names.test.ts:6–12` runs `execSync("task --version")` without a timeout and catches every error as `taskAvailable = false`. All tests subsequently use that availability flag to skip.

**Failure mode:** Leaving the probe outside R3 preserves an unbounded subprocess. Merely adding a timeout inside the existing catch converts a hung installed tool into an apparently successful suite of skipped tests. Either outcome violates P3.

**Disposition consequence:** R3 can bind with explicit coverage of the availability probe: use the bounded runner there too, skip only for an identified missing executable, and propagate timeout diagnostics. Handle both returned `spawnSync` errors and thrown synchronous-exec errors if both APIs remain.

The diagnostic should say the command exceeded the limit and was terminated; it should not claim that every descendant was killed.

### 3. sharpens-framing — The first acceptance criterion contradicts the proposed fixture

**Evidence:** The existing version-bearing invocation is at `taskfile_release_names.test.ts:83–111`; the production command template is at `Taskfile.yml:806`. R1 replaces that invocation with another `task … release -- 0.0.0 …`, targeting the temporary Taskfile.

**Failure mode:** The literal criterion “No test … runs `task release` with a version argument” rejects the intended replacement even though it avoids the production pipeline.

**Disposition consequence:** Narrow the criterion to prohibit version-bearing invocation of the **repository’s real release task/pipeline**, while expressly permitting the isolated stub fixture. The mechanism can otherwise bind.

### 4. footnote — The fixture preserves the relevant transport boundary

`tasks/engine.yml:69–72` transports the command through JSON; both runtime branches call the same wrapper (`:107–114`). `tasks/engine-invoke.cjs:349–364` decodes and splits it before spawning. Existing splitter tests (`tasks/engine-invoke.test.cjs:84–90,185–200`) do not exercise go-task’s template rendering.

Reading the real release `ENGINE_CMD` is therefore worthwhile. It avoids a copied template silently diverging, provided extraction selects the release task specifically and fails when that structure disappears. The fixture covers the shared quoting boundary, not framework-source pin resolution.

Answers to the four Stop 1 questions:

1. **Enough to justify the fix, not enough to claim a proven root cause.** Pinned `pipeline.ts:372–381` confirms dry-run does not execute that CI step. Describe the change as removing expensive integration work and bounding subprocess waits; the exact hang source remains unknown.
2. **Yes, structurally.** R1 exercises the boundary responsible for the single-quote-wrap regression. Keep the real command template. Linux/Windows equivalence remains a verification item: record the positive and quote-mutated negative runs on Linux CI; the supplied Windows prototype is supporting evidence, not Linux proof.
3. **Plausible, but unverified by this review.** The wrapper uses inherited stdio (`engine-invoke.cjs:386–400`), making the descendant-held-pipe scenario relevant. A bounded Linux experiment with that process shape should confirm return time and the actual timeout diagnostic before claiming P3 proven. This does not require a new CI gate.
4. **Change it too**, for the reason in finding 1. Preserve a truthful dispatch assertion without retaining the build/pin chain in this file.

## Problem

`packages/core/src/content-contracts/standards/taskfile_release_names.test.ts` can hang the CI merge gate (`task check:merge`). Its #2547 test runs a full `task release -- 0.0.0 --dry-run --skip-tag --skip-release --summary "test what's next"`: go-task, the `ts:build` dependency (`pnpm run build`), `engine:invoke`, then the pinned runtime. It uses `spawnSync` with no timeout.

Evidence (2026-11-20):

- Of the 43 latest completed merge-gate jobs (Blacksmith primary), 42 finished in 12 min or less (median 6.4 min). In a sampled normal job (136352833330) this file took 4254 ms.
- Twice it did not finish. Run 44683125022 was cancelled at the 6 h job limit with 1621 of 1622 files done and only this file in flight. Pin PR #6861 (run 44763201751) was in the same state after 50 min. In the cancelled run, the log shows the `release -- --help` call completed. The only calls left after it are a go-task `--list-all` and the #2547 dry run.
- The dry run does not run a nested `task check`. With `--dry-run`, step 5 only prints `DRYRUN (would run task ci:local ...)`. Locally the call took 27 s, about 25 s of it a cold `tsc -b` from the `ts:build` dependency.
- Which process in that chain blocks is not known. At the 6 h cancel, a node, node, sh chain was still alive. `spawnSync` waits until every holder of the child's output pipes exits, and the vitest test timeout cannot interrupt a synchronous call.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] No test in `taskfile_release_names.test.ts` runs `task release` with a version argument.
- [ ] A #2547 test runs real go-task with the real `tasks/engine.yml`, `tasks/engine-invoke.cjs` and release `ENGINE_CMD` against a stub bin, and asserts that `test what's next` arrives as one argv element.
- [ ] Changing `tasks/engine.yml` to wrap `ENGINE_CMD` in single quotes (the pre-#2547 shape) makes that test fail. The PR records that run.
- [ ] Every `task` spawn in the file has a timeout. On timeout the test fails with a message that names the command and the limit.
- [ ] The file finishes in under 10 s in CI. The PR records its vitest time before (4254 ms in job 136352833330; hung in run 44683125022) and after (from the PR's own merge-gate log).

Refs #2547, #6849
